correctness.rationale: For \(v_b=(1,\zeta^s,\zeta^t)\), normalized tightness is equivalent to three vanishing character moments. All three moments of the four-node family equal \(w_0+(1+2\cos(2\pi a/p))w_*\), which vanishes with positive normalized weights whenever \(p/3<a<2p/3\). A hypothetical three-node Parseval system forces equal weights \(1/3\), contrary to irreducibility of \(\Phi_p\) for primes \(p\ge5\). With rational weights, the first-coordinate marginal must equal \(1/p\) at every residue, requiring at least \(p\) nodes. Equality forces weights \(1/p\), and the remaining moments hold precisely when both \(f\) and \(t\mapsto t-f(t)\) are permutations. The explicit example \(f(t)=2t\) works. Translated-design distinctness and all quantified cases follow from algebra, while fourteen finite frame calculations are corroboration only.
